t: You're looking at a set of garden statues and a cistern in the grounds of Fenton House, in Camden. They were made by John Cheere, an English sculptor born in London in 1709. He was the younger brother of another sculptor, Sir Henry Cheere. Before he took up sculpture, he was apprenticed as a haberdasher, from 1725 to 1732. So these figures and the cistern are the work of a man who started out in a very different trade.
